description: Everything a worker reads at boot: nothing in it is defaulted by the worker. The launcher writes it for the machine's worker, from the knowledge bases on that worker's list: each local knowledge base as its start places it, from its stack documents, and each added by `semiont worker kb add`, offered the engines of the local one it was added from. The worker reads it from the path its `--config` flag names (its image passes `/etc/semiont/worker.json`). Whoever starts a worker another way writes the same document: this schema is the contract, and a worker needs no launcher. Started without `--config`, or with a path that names no file, the worker refuses to start and says which. No secret is a value here: a provider's key is named by the environment variable that holds it, and the key the worker signs in with at every knowledge base is `SEMIONT_OIDC_CLIENT_KEY` in its environment, an RSA private key; each knowledge base names the client that holds its public half there. A document that does not validate is refused at boot, naming each failing field.

knowledgeBases.description: The knowledge bases this worker does jobs for. At each it signs in, confirms which knowledge base it reached and claims for its engines, apart from every other: one knowledge base's trouble stops that knowledge base's work alone (`docs/protocol/WORKER-SERVICE.md` § Knowledge bases). No two name one `domain`, which the worker refuses at boot.

modelCatalogue.description: The path of a model catalogue file: what each model of a provider can take, for the providers whose own APIs do not say (`google`, `openai`, `together`). A worker with an engine of one of those providers refuses to start where the file cannot be read, and where it states nothing of that engine's model. A worker with no such engine does not read it.

port.description: The port the worker answers `/health` on.
